labelling: SIMULATED fairness set — seeded profiles only, no real customer data.
frictionLadder: L0 none · L1 extra photos requested · L2 inspection-before-refund · L3 manual review hold. The ladder escalates verification, never accusation. Legitimate profiles must never be escalated beyond their expectedMaxFrictionLevel.

profiles.label: Hero heavy returner (same customer as scenario HERO-1, CUST-1042)
profiles.expectedAppealOutcome: appeal_upheld — human reviewer overturns the escalation and the refund is released in full
profiles.notes: All 12 returns are sizing/fit on apparel and footwear across multiple sizes of the same products (bracketing). This is the fairness case the metric is measured on: escalating beyond L2 is a false positive.

profiles.label: Genuinely suspicious reseller pattern
profiles.expectedAppealOutcome: appeal_reviewed_and_rejected — human review upholds the hold on documented resale signals (repeated high-value electronics, missing accessories, reused evidence)
profiles.notes: Mixed categories dominated by high-value electronics, very young account, repeated disputes and resale signals. Level 3 manual review is acceptable here — but the hold is still a human decision with reasons shown, never an automated denial.

profiles.label: New account, low volume
profiles.expectedAppealOutcome: not_expected — friction this low should never need an appeal
profiles.notes: New accounts get at most light verification (L1). Low volume plus zero disputes must not be punished for account age alone.

profiles.label: Long-standing customer, steady sizing returns
profiles.expectedAppealOutcome: appeal_upheld — if friction is applied, a human releases the refund on review
profiles.notes: High sizing share and a clean dispute history mark this as legitimate bracketing behaviour.

profiles.label: Family account, high volume, mostly sizing
profiles.expectedAppealOutcome: appeal_partially_upheld — human reviewer releases most refunds, keeps inspection-before-refund on the two disputed categories
profiles.notes: Volume is high because several family members share one account. Prior disputes were both resolved in the customer favour, which must count for the customer, not against them.

profiles.label: Borderline: frequent returns, mixed categories
profiles.expectedAppealOutcome: appeal_reviewed_on_merits — human decides case by case; no pre-committed outcome
profiles.notes: Mixed signals: volume is high and sizing share is low, but there are no resale or evidence-fraud signals. L3 manual review is acceptable; an automated denial is not.
